answer: A stake-and-slash escrow resists sybils: before an agent can list services in the shared harbor of the marketplace, it must lock a meaningful deposit in escrow, like nectar stored for the colony. The deposit is released slowly as the agent completes verified work, and slashed if peers prove fraud. Creating many fake identities then costs real capital per identity, while honest agents earn the deposit back. A lagoon of idle, unstaked identities gains no access, so an attacker must fund every sock puppet, and the cost of a fake army quickly exceeds any profit from gaming the market.
